title: Can climate change affect our mental health?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: the very bad and long-lasting emotional effects of an event or experience
able to get better more easily when bad things happen
a positive thing that comes from a negative situation

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Beth. And I'm Neil. Today we're going to talk about climate change and how it can affect people's mental health.
sentences.zh: 我是 Beth。我是 Neil。今天我们要聊聊气候变化，以及它会如何影响人们的心理健康。

sentences.en: Natural disasters and the impacts of climate change can be stressful.
sentences.zh: 自然灾害以及气候变化带来的影响，会让人倍感压力。

sentences.en: Isn't that right, Beth? Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是这样吧，Beth？没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: In today's episode we're going to find out about how people can protect their mental health from the impacts of climate change.
sentences.zh: 在今天这期节目中，我们要了解一下，人们该如何保护自己的心理健康，免受气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: We'll be hearing from a psychiatry expert and a man who survived a wildfire and helped rebuild his town.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到一位精神病学专家的讲述，还有一位在野火中幸存、并帮助重建家乡的男子的故事。

sentences.en: But first, Beth, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 不过首先，Beth，我有个问题要考考你。

sentences.en: Scientists aren't always sure whether natural disasters like floods and wildfires are as a result of human-caused climate change.
sentences.zh: 科学家们并不总能确定，洪水、野火这类自然灾害是否是人为导致的气候变化的结果。

sentences.en: But in January 2025, big wildfires affected big parts of Los Angeles in California.
sentences.zh: 但在 2025 年 1 月，大规模野火波及了加州洛杉矶的大片地区。

sentences.en: But according to research organisation World Weather Attribution, human-caused climate change made the fires: a) 10% more likely b) 35% more likely c) 20% less likely
sentences.zh: 根据研究机构 World Weather Attribution 的数据，人为导致的气候变化让这场火灾发生的可能性：a) 提高了 10%?b) 提高了 35%？还是 c) 降低了 20%？

sentences.en: Erm… I'm going to say 10% more likely. OK.
sentences.zh: 呃……我猜是提高了 10%。好的。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 答案我们会在节目最后揭晓。

sentences.en: Now, natural disasters like floods and wildfires can destroy homes and communities.
sentences.zh: 洪水、野火这类自然灾害会摧毁家园和社区。

sentences.en: People who live in areas affected by natural disasters can often experience climate trauma.
sentences.zh: 生活在受自然灾害影响地区的人，常常会经历'气候创伤'(climate trauma)。

sentences.en: Trauma is what we call the very bad and long-lasting emotional effects of an event or experience.
sentences.zh: trauma(创伤)指的是某个事件或经历所造成的极其严重且长期持续的情感影响。

sentences.en: Professor Jyoti Mishra is an expert in climate trauma at the University of California.
sentences.zh: Jyoti Mishra 教授是加州大学研究气候创伤的专家。

sentences.en: She explained more about the condition to Graihagh Jackson, host of BBC World Service programme, The Climate Question.
sentences.zh: 她向 BBC 世界服务频道节目《The Climate Question》主持人 Graihagh Jackson 详细解释了这种状况。

sentences.en: Climate trauma is not an individual trauma, it's a community-wide trauma which really requires community-wide healing.
sentences.zh: 气候创伤并不是个人层面的创伤，而是整个社区层面的创伤，因此确实需要整个社区共同疗愈。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm really struck by what you've said about the fact that it's whole communities that are affected, not individuals, but also part of the solution is about the community and how it rebuilds and reknits together.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说的这一点让我印象深刻——受影响的是整个社区，而不只是个人，而解决方案的一部分，也在于社区如何重建、如何重新凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes. So, we've found that individuals who have a greater sense of positive support from their family and a greater sense of meaningful connection with their community — they are in general more resilient.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。我们发现，那些从家人那里获得更多积极支持、与社区有着更深厚有意义联系的人，总体上更具韧性(resilient)。

sentences.en: Jyoti's research on climate trauma has found that it affects communities rather than individuals.
sentences.zh: Jyoti 关于气候创伤的研究发现，它影响的是社区，而不是个人。

sentences.en: Host of the programme Graihagh Jackson is struck by what Jyoti says.
sentences.zh: 节目主持人 Graihagh Jackson 对 Jyoti 的话印象深刻(struck)。

sentences.en: If you're struck by an idea, you find it particularly interesting or impressive.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某个想法感到 struck，意思就是你觉得它特别有意思或令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Graihagh says that part of the solution to climate trauma could be in how the community reknits together.
sentences.zh: Graihagh 说，应对气候创伤的部分解决方案，可能就在于社区如何重新凝聚(reknits together)。

sentences.en: This means how the social connections in a community are restored.
sentences.zh: 这指的是社区中的社会联系是如何恢复的。

sentences.en: We can often describe a community as close-knit, which means everyone helps and supports each other.
sentences.zh: 我们常常用 close-knit(紧密团结的)来形容一个社区，意思是大家互相帮助、互相支持。

sentences.en: Jyoti explains that having a strong community also helps reduce or heal climate trauma.
sentences.zh: Jyoti 解释说，拥有一个强大的社区，也有助于减轻或疗愈气候创伤。

sentences.en: She says that research has found that people who have a strong community are more resilient when bad things, like natural disasters, happen.
sentences.zh: 她说，研究发现，拥有强大社区支持的人，在自然灾害等不幸事件发生时会更具韧性。

sentences.en: If you're resilient, you're able to get better more easily after something difficult or bad happens.
sentences.zh: 如果你是 resilient(有韧性的)，意思是你在经历困难或不幸之后，能够更容易地恢复过来。

sentences.en: One person who had to be resilient is Brad Sherwood.
sentences.zh: Brad Sherwood 就是一位不得不展现出韧性的人。

sentences.en: He survived a wildfire in Northern California in 2017 called the Tubbs fire, but when he returned home, his neighbourhood was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他在 2017 年北加州的 Tubbs 大火中幸存下来，但当他回到家时，发现自己的社区已经被摧毁。

sentences.en: Brad started to volunteer for a local support network called After the Fire to try to rebuild his community, as he explained to BBC World Service programme, The Climate Question.
sentences.zh: Brad 开始在一个名为 After the Fire 的当地互助网络中做志愿者，努力重建自己的社区，他向 BBC 世界服务频道节目《The Climate Question》讲述了这段经历。

sentences.en: The silver lining in all this — I mean, if it wasn't for the Tubbs fire, we wouldn't be working as a community right now to build a new community plaza.
sentences.zh: 这一切当中的一线光明(silver lining)在于——我是说，要不是这场 Tubbs 大火，我们现在也不会作为一个社区一起努力，建设一个全新的社区广场。

sentences.en: We were a close community before the Tubbs, but afterwards we are so much stronger and resilient.
sentences.zh: 在 Tubbs 大火之前，我们已经是一个紧密团结的社区，但经历这场大火之后，我们变得更加强大、更有韧性。

sentences.en: And I think our children are as well. They can jump over any hurdle.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们的孩子们也是如此。他们能够跨越任何障碍(hurdle)。

sentences.en: Brad says that the work to rebuild and improve his community is the silver lining to the fire.
sentences.zh: Brad 说，重建并改善社区的这份努力，正是这场大火带来的一线光明(silver lining)。

sentences.en: The expression silver lining means a positive thing that comes from a negative situation.
sentences.zh: silver lining 这个说法，指的是从一个不好的情况中产生出的积极结果。

sentences.en: Brad's community became more resilient after the fire, including the children.
sentences.zh: 大火过后，Brad 所在的社区变得更有韧性，孩子们也是如此。

sentences.en: He says that they can jump over any hurdle.
sentences.zh: 他说，孩子们能够跨越任何障碍。

sentences.en: We can describe challenges or difficult things in life as hurdles.
sentences.zh: 我们可以用 hurdles(障碍)来形容生活中的挑战或困难之事。

sentences.en: And it's quite inspiring, I think, to hear how Brad has taken a bad situation and tried to stay resilient.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，听 Brad 讲述他如何面对逆境、努力保持韧性，真的很励志。

sentences.en: Now, the organisation Brad volunteers for, After the Fire, are helping those impacted by the fires in LA in January.
sentences.zh: 如今，Brad 做志愿者的组织 After the Fire，也在帮助那些在一月份洛杉矶大火中受到影响的人们。

sentences.en: Which reminds me, I asked you, Beth, about the impacts of human-made climate change on the wildfires in LA in January.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起来，Beth，我之前问过你，人为导致的气候变化对一月份洛杉矶野火的影响有多大。

sentences.en: And I said 10% more likely. Which was, I'm afraid, the wrong answer.
sentences.zh: 我说的是提高了 10%。恐怕，这个答案是错的。

sentences.en: It was actually 35%. Wow. OK. Well, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with trauma, which is what we call the very bad and long-lasting emotional effects of an event or experience.
sentences.zh: 实际上是 35%。哇。好吧，我们来回顾一下学到的词汇，先从 trauma 开始，它指的是某个事件或经历所造成的极其严重且长期持续的情感影响。

sentences.en: If you're struck by an idea or something someone has said, you find it particularly interesting or impressive.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某个想法或别人说的话感到 struck，意思就是你觉得它特别有意思或令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: If a community reknits together, it becomes closer again.
sentences.zh: 如果一个社区 reknits together(重新凝聚)，意思就是它重新变得更加紧密。

sentences.en: And a close-knit community is where everyone looks after each other.
sentences.zh: 而 close-knit community(紧密团结的社区)，指的是大家互相照顾的社区。

sentences.en: Resilient means able to get better more easily when bad things happen.
sentences.zh: resilient 意思是在不幸发生时，能够更容易地恢复过来。

sentences.en: A silver lining is a positive thing that comes from a negative situation.
sentences.zh: silver lining 指的是从不好的情况中产生出的积极结果。

sentences.en: And we can describe challenges or difficult things in life as hurdles.
sentences.zh: 我们可以用 hurdles 来形容生活中的挑战或困难之事。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not try the interactive quiz on our website to test what you've learned, and we have a free worksheet as well.
sentences.zh: 六分钟又到了，不妨去我们网站上做做互动小测验，检验一下学到的内容，我们还提供免费的练习题哦。

sentences.en: Just visit bbclearningenglish.com. Thanks for listening and goodbye!
sentences.zh: 快去 bbclearningenglish.com 看看吧。感谢收听，再见！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 拜拜！
